title: Tempering and few-shot calibration of pathology foundation models improve digital biomarker reproducibility across slide scanners
abstract: arXiv:2611.31536v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Pathology foundation models underpin a growing number of histology-based cancer biomarkers, but sensitivity to slide scanner-specific image signatures degrades cross-center reliability and reproducibility. We developed a foundation model fine-tuning method that improved consistency in head-and-neck cancer human papillomavirus (HPV) prediction, colorectal cancer microsatellite instability (MSI) identification, prostate cancer grading and breast cancer phenotyping. This tempering method decreased cross-scanner prediction differences by 67.5% for HPV (95% CI 59.0-73.9%), 69.3% for MSI (95% CI 51.9-76.5%) and 63.4%-81.2% for breast signatures. Cross-scanner prostate grade agreement rose from 42.5% to 92.7%. Under full scanner-HPV confounding during training, AUROC fell from 0.80 to 0.68 with original model features but only from 0.86 to 0.84 with tempering. translated_title: 病理基础模型的调和与少样本校准提高数字生物标志物在不同切片扫描仪间的可重复性
translated_abstract: 病理基础模型支撑着越来越多基于组织学的癌症生物标志物，但其对切片扫描仪特异性图像特征的敏感性会降低跨中心的可靠性与可重复性。我们开发了一种基础模型微调方法，提高了头颈癌人乳头瘤病毒（HPV）预测、结直肠癌微卫星不稳定（MSI）识别、前列腺癌分级以及乳腺癌表型分型的一致性。这种“调和”方法使HPV的跨扫描仪预测差异降低了67.5%（95% CI 59.0-73.9%），MSI降低了69.3%（95% CI 51.9-76.5%），乳腺癌特征降低了63.4%-81.2%。跨扫描仪的前列腺癌分级一致性从42.5%提升至92.7%。在训练中存在完全的扫描仪-HPV混杂时，使用原始模型特征的AUROC从0.80降至0.68，而使用调和方法仅从0.86降至0.84。与事后特征校准不同，调和方法仅使用公开数据即可达到相当或更好的效果。
tldr: 该研究提出一种仅需公开数据的“调和”微调方法，可显著降低病理基础模型对扫描仪差异的敏感性，大幅提升HPV预测、MSI识别、前列腺癌分级等数字生物标志物的跨扫描仪可重复性。
en_tdlr: This study introduces a tempering fine-tuning method that uses only public data to substantially reduce pathology foundation models' sensitivity to scanner-specific image signatures, greatly improving cross-scanner reproducibility of digital biomarkers such as HPV prediction, MSI identification, and prostate cancer grading.
